evidence.summary: FAQ is a hard-coded list of {q, a} entries with one entry (password reset)
suggest(text) lower-cases and splits on whitespace, then returns every FAQ whose question shares at least one word, in list order

architecture.backend: one Python module with a static list and a matching function; no server, storage or UI

features.name: FAQ answer suggestion
features.description: Given free text, suggest the FAQ entries that may answer it
features.observed_behaviour: word-set intersection between the text and each FAQ question; any shared word is a match; results are not ranked
features.business_logic: case-insensitive; punctuation is not stripped (so 'password?' and 'password' differ); common words such as 'how', 'do', 'i' match, so almost any question matches; no limit on results

features.name: FAQ content
features.description: A list of question and answer pairs
features.observed_behaviour: hard-coded in the module; one entry; no way to add, edit or remove entries at run time

entities.name: FAQ
entities.description: a frequently asked question and its answer

rules.value: at least one shared lower-cased whitespace-separated word

unknowns: How the widget is shown to end users (the user calls it an FAQ widget; no UI code exists in sources/faqbot)
Where the real FAQ content lives and who maintains it: only one hard-coded entry exists
Actual runtime behaviour: the code was read, not run (running source code is not approved)
